title: Future of Disclosure / Quest for Bigfoot
excerpt: Author and researcher Mike Bara discussed the state of UFO disclosure and alleged alien encounters. Followed by ecologist Robert Pyle, who outlined decades of field research he's gathered while looking for Bigfoot.
content:
About the show

In the first half, author and researcher Mike Bara discussed the state of UFO disclosure and alleged alien encounters. He cautioned that the shift in political power following the midterm elections could derail recent congressional interest in UFOs. Bara predicted ongoing public hearings would come to an end, potentially leaving researchers with either a multi-year hiatus or an expedited release of classified files before new leadership takes hold. He also remained skeptical of former intelligence officers David Grusch and Jay Stratton, despite their prominence in the disclosure debate. "Ultimately they're just telling us stories," he remarked.

Bara argued the public still lacked physical evidence that could be independently examined, such as material "definitely not of human origin." He warned listeners not to "deify" intelligence figures, adding that disclosure may reflect "what the government wants you to believe is the truth," rather than the full truth. He proceeded to trace presidential UFO briefings back to Harry Truman and the MJ-12 documents, which reportedly detail investigations of alien spacecraft during Truman's administration. Bara also connected Richard Nixon's removal from office to a reported encounter with aliens. "It was literally a CIA coup against the president," he explained, claiming the effort began shortly after Nixon allegedly showed entertainer Jackie Gleason alien bodies at Homestead Air Force Base.

Addressing more recent reports, Bara discussed the 2023 Las Vegas "backyard alien incident." He stated local law enforcement body cameras recorded an unidentified aerial object without a heat signature, ruling out a conventional meteor. Bara further claimed that police officers abruptly shut off their cameras upon entering the yard due to what was present on site. "You will never see that body cam footage because of what's on it... [so] you figure it out," he said.

----------------

In the second half, ecologist Robert Pyle outlined decades of field research he's gathered while looking for Bigfoot. He framed his stance on Bigfoot through the lens of a rational biologist. Rather than viewing the creature as supernatural, he categorized it as an undiscovered primate. "I believe that the Bigfoot, like us, is a species of ape, and that we have common ancestors," Pyle stated. When asked about his personal conviction regarding its existence, he placed himself at "95 percent" certainty based on tracks he's documented and a brief personal sighting in the Cascade Mountains.

However, his scientific rigor prevents him from reaching absolute certainty without definitive physical proof. "I have not yet seen the DNA, and I have not had a sighting of the quality that it would take to completely convince me," Pyle explained. Placing Bigfoot on the evolutionary tree, he reasoned the creature would likely rank "closer to humans than it would be to the other apes," possibly with a larger cranial capacity than our own. "Who's to say which is the superior ape?" he mused. "It might be considered by primatologists to be more advanced than humans."

Pyle addressed the Patterson-Gimlin film and the allegations that it's a hoax. He admitted he remained cautious yet still found aspects of the footage difficult to dismiss. He claimed frame-by-frame analysis appeared to show "the muscles bunching in the leg," the "arch of the foot bending," and other details he believed would be hard to fake. Even if the film were proven fraudulent, Pyle asserted it would not erase the broader body of reports, tracks, casts, and eyewitness accounts.
